correctness.rationale: Each of the 375 explicitly parametrized lines has exactly two or four nonzero coordinates. Two-coordinate points are 10 coordinate pairs times five fifth-root labels, each on 15 lines; at a four-coordinate common point, two complementary pairings of opposite fifth powers are possible precisely for the (A,A,-A,-A) sign pattern, yielding 5 omitted positions times three sign partitions times 5^3 fifth-root assignments = 1875 points, exactly two lines each. The 375 lines give 5250+1875=7125 edges and valency 38. The complete standard-library congruence enumerator checks all 70125 unordered pairs, all common-neighbor values (13 and 1), the complete fifty 15-line pencils, and the component graph KG(5,2) blown up by five independent vertices. A separately constructed rank computation over F_11 agrees on all 70125 decisions and serves only as an implementation cross-check, not a proof by reduction. The mathematical support argument establishes completeness in characteristic zero.

originality.rationale: The inspected primary sources Albano--Katz (1991) and Pauli (arXiv:2006.12089, section 6) give the 50 Fano-curve components and 375 crossing lines in the parameter scheme, but no complete pairwise ambient-intersection census for these line images. Their Fano-curve intersections are not equivalent to intersection of two parameterized lines in P^4. The new result adds 1875 ambient double points, two edge-type common-neighbor values, and recovery of all 50 parameter curves as maximal cliques. Katz--Morrison (2022) concerns mirror quotient geometry, not an incidence theorem for the original 375 lines. Focused index searches for exact counts, aliases and graph reductions returned only different problems, which is not standalone proof of novelty. Older unindexed incidence work remains a bibliographic risk.

value.rationale: The 375 distinguished projective lines are the canonical crossings of the 50 Fano parameter curves on an especially symmetric smooth quintic, not an arbitrary finite sample. Two geometrically different incidences are naturally available: intersections of parameter curves in the Fano scheme and intersections of the corresponding line images in P^4. The complete 50 fifteenfold plus 1875 double ambient-point structure and intrinsic recovery of the original 50 cone-families from the ambient line graph explain their relationship. The 13-versus-1 common-neighbor distinction is a structural certificate that reconstructs geometric families without using coordinates; this is a meaningful natural classification, not a routine isolated count. Nothing is claimed about general quintics, virtual Euler contributions or a downstream deformation theorem.
